correctness.rationale: For bounded A=A*>=aI and B=B*, the norm Fréchet derivative of (A²+i t[A,B]+t²B²)^{1/2} solves AL+LA=i[A,B] via Sylvester inverse ∫e^{-uA}De^{-uA}du. Lipschitzness of self-adjoint positive-part norm gives d_±(t)=t||(±L)_+||+O(t²). In finite dimensions nonzero traceless L has both signs. For unilateral shift S, A=2I+(S+S*)/2>=I, X=I-(S-S*)/(2i), B=AX+XA, exact commutator i[A,X]=-P0/2 gives d_+(t)=O(t²), d_-(t)=t/2+O(t²). Approximate constant unit vectors v_N at the top spectral endpoint give ||A+i t B||>=3sqrt(1+4t²) and d_+(t)>=3(sqrt(1+4t²)-1), hence exact quadratic order. For nilpotent finite S_n, L_n=(P_last-P0)/2 has both one-sided slopes 1/2 for n>=2. Independent NumPy matrices for n=2,3,6,20 verified this commutator and Sylvester equation to machine precision; finite tests are not proof of infinite rank.
